guides.title: How to Choose Wireless Earbuds in 2026
guides.excerpt: ANC, battery life, fit and price — what actually matters when buying wireless earbuds on Amazon, with our pick from the ZayPick catalog.
guides.content:
Wireless earbuds all look similar in photos, but four things decide whether you will actually enjoy them: noise cancellation, fit, battery life and price. This guide explains each one in plain language, using real products from the ZayPick catalog.

## Noise cancellation (ANC)

Active noise cancellation uses microphones to cancel low, steady sounds such as bus engines and office hum. It helps a lot on flights and commutes, but it cannot silence sudden loud sounds. If you mostly listen at home, good passive sealing from the ear tips may be enough, and you can save money.

## Fit matters more than brand

Earbuds that fall out are useless, whatever the brand. Look for multiple ear-tip sizes in the box and a shape that suits your ears. In-ear buds with silicone tips seal better and give stronger bass; open-ear buds feel lighter and let in more outside sound.

## Battery life to check

- Earbuds alone: 5 to 8 hours per charge is normal for ANC earbuds.
- Case total: 24 to 30 hours with the charging case is good.
- Fast charging: a 5-minute charge giving 1 hour of playback is a useful bonus, not a must-have.

## What to check before you buy

- Rating and review count on Amazon — a 4.4-star product with 18,000+ reviews is a safer bet than a 5-star product with 50 reviews.
- Bluetooth version and codec support for your phone.
- Water resistance (IPX4 or better) if you run or work out.
- Whether the price is a real discount — compare the price with the old price shown on the product page.

## Our pick

The Apple AirPods Pro 3 (ASIN B0FQFB8FMG) are our pick from this guide: $150, was $249, 4.4 stars from 18,255 reviews (price as of 2026-11-23). They offer up to 2x more noise cancellation than AirPods Pro 2, Live Translation, heart-rate sensing, up to 8 hours of listening with ANC on, IP57 sweat and rain resistance, and 5 ear-tip sizes. If you want a cheaper on-ear option, the Beats Solo 4 (ASIN B0FHLPS8ZF) is $79.99, was $199.95, 4.6 stars from 29,366 reviews, with up to 50 hours of battery life. guides.title: How to Choose a Streaming Stick for Your TV
guides.excerpt: HD vs 4K, Wi-Fi, voice remote and price — how to pick the right streaming stick for your TV without paying for features you will not use.
guides.content:
A streaming stick turns an old TV into a smart TV for the price of a dinner out. The choice is simpler than it looks: match the stick to your TV and your internet, then pick the cheapest one that covers both.

## HD or 4K?

- Your TV is 1080p only: an HD stick is enough. A 4K stick will still work, but you will not see the extra resolution.
- Your TV is 4K: buy a 4K stick with HDR (Dolby Vision or HDR10+) so films look their best.
- You mostly watch free and live TV: any modern stick covers that.

## Wi-Fi and speed

Streaming sticks need stable Wi-Fi more than raw speed. Wi-Fi 6 helps in busy homes with many devices. If your TV is far from the router, a stick with long-range Wi-Fi or an Ethernet adapter option is worth it.

## Voice remote and interface

- A voice remote saves a lot of typing when searching for shows.
- Check that your favourite apps (Netflix, Disney+, Prime Video, Hulu, Apple TV) are supported — most sticks support all of them.
- Some interfaces show more ads than others; that is a fair trade for a lower price.

## What to check before you buy

- Resolution of your TV (1080p vs 4K).
- Storage: 8 GB is standard and fine for streaming apps.
- Rating and review count — the Fire TV Stick 4K Plus has 4.6 stars from 116,771 reviews, which is a strong signal.
- Price vs old price: streaming sticks go on deep sale often, so do not pay full price if you can wait for a deal.

## Our pick

It streams 4K Ultra HD with Dolby Vision, HDR10+ and Dolby Atmos, has Wi-Fi 6, AI-powered Fire TV Search, and an Alexa Voice Remote. If your TV is only 1080p, the Roku Streaming Stick HD (ASIN B0DXXYS4BJ) is $19, was $39.99, 4.6 stars from 26,566 reviews, and the Fire TV Stick HD (ASIN B0DJGDC3BD) is $15.99, was $39.99, 4.2 stars from 8,172 reviews. guides.title: How to Choose an Insulated Water Bottle or Tumbler
guides.excerpt: Size, lid, insulation and cup-holder fit — what to check before buying an insulated bottle or tumbler on Amazon.
guides.content:
A good insulated bottle keeps drinks cold for hours and does not leak in your bag. The right size depends on where you use it most: desk, car, gym or hiking.

## Size first

- 24 oz is light and fits most cup holders — good for a desk or a short trip.
- 32 oz is the sweet spot for most people: enough water for hours without being too heavy.
- 40 oz is best for long days and workouts, but it is heavy when full and does not fit every cup holder.

## Lid and leak test

- A straw lid is best for sipping while driving or working.
- A flip-straw or screw cap is better for tossing the bottle in a bag.
- Check the reviews for leak reports — a bottle that leaks is useless, however good its insulation is.

## Insulation and material

- Double-wall or triple-wall vacuum insulation keeps drinks cold for 12 to 24 hours.
- Stainless steel lasts longer than plastic and does not hold flavours.
- BPA-free matters if you drink from it every day.
- Dishwasher-safe saves time; hand-wash-only bottles get dirty fast.

## What to check before you buy

- Capacity in ounces, and whether it fits your car cup holder.
- Rating and review count — the STANLEY Quencher has 4.7 stars from 208,034 reviews.
- Price vs old price, and whether the price changes by color.
- Whether a handle is included — a 32 oz or 40 oz bottle without a handle is hard to carry.

In everyday use, the job is simple: warm water, a little dish soap, and a few passes around the inside walls and base. The long handle gives you leverage, and the bristle head is wide enough to scrub the sides in one motion, yet narrow enough to pass through a standard Hydro Flask mouth. That balance is why many buyers keep coming back to this brush after cheaper ones bend, shed bristles, or snap at the handle. For daily users, though, the steel handle and long reach solve the two problems that kill most bottle brushes: bending and falling short of the bottom.

guides.title: Garmin Venu X1 Review: A Big-Screen Smartwatch Worth $499.99?
guides.excerpt: Our Garmin Venu X1 review looks at its 2-inch AMOLED display, 8-day battery, health tracking, and whether the $499.99 smartwatch is worth it.
guides.content:
The Garmin Venu X1 looks like a Garmin that decided to stop apologising for its screen. It is square, slim, and built around a 2-inch AMOLED display, which is the largest Garmin has put in a watch of this kind. This Garmin Venu X1 review looks at what that big screen buys you, what it costs in battery life, and whether the current $499.99 price makes it a smart buy. We have not tested the watch ourselves, so everything below comes from Garmin specs, retailer listings, and published reviews from Tech Advisor, Android Central, and Tom's Guide.

## Garmin Venu X1 Display and Design

The display is the reason most people will notice this watch. It measures 2 inches diagonally, with a 448 x 486 pixel AMOLED touchscreen under sapphire crystal. Reviewers describe it as bright and easy to read indoors and outdoors, and maps and workout data have far more room than on a round 1.4-inch Venu. The case is 41 x 46 x 7.9 mm, which makes it Garmin's thinnest watch at about 8 mm, and the case alone weighs 34 grams, or 40 grams with the ComfortFit nylon band. The caseback is titanium, the rest of the case is fibre-reinforced polymer, and the watch is rated 5ATM for water resistance. It also has a built-in LED flashlight, a speaker and microphone for calls, and two buttons, which is a change from the three-button layout on the Venu 3. It comes in Black and Moss, both with a nylon strap.

## Garmin Venu X1 Health and Fitness Tracking

Under the big screen, the Venu X1 is still a full Garmin. It tracks HRV status, sleep with coaching and a sleep score, Body Battery energy monitoring, stress, and Pulse Ox blood oxygen. For training, it offers more than 100 preloaded sports apps, including running, golf, and strength training, plus built-in mapping and navigation, music storage, and Garmin Pay. The watch uses Garmin's Elevate v5 heart rate sensor, and Tech Advisor praised its heart rate monitoring in particular. Android Central noted that an August 2025 update added running tools from the Forerunner 970, which helps close the gap with Garmin's more serious training watches. If you want a watch that covers daily health, sleep, and a wide mix of workouts, the Venu X1 has the depth to do it.

## Garmin Venu X1 Battery Life

Battery life is where the big screen asks for a trade. Garmin rates the Venu X1 for up to 8 days in smartwatch mode, or 2 days with the display always on, and up to 11 days in battery saver mode. GPS use is rated at up to 16 hours in GPS-only mode, 14 hours with all satellite systems, and 7 hours with all systems plus music. That is strong next to an Apple Watch, which lasts about a day or two, but it is short next to other Garmins. The Venu 3, for example, is rated for up to 14 days in smartwatch mode. Tom's Guide found the Venu X1 could beat its always-on estimate in real use, at just over two days with about an hour of running a day, but the point stands: if you turn the screen on all the time, plan on charging every couple of days.

## Garmin Venu X1 Price: Is $499.99 Worth It?

The Venu X1 launched in June 2025 at $799.99 in the US. At the time of writing, retailer listings show it at $499.99, including Bloomingdale's, which lists it at $499.99 against a $699.99 price, and other retailers at the same $499.99 level. That is a big drop from launch, and it changes the value question. At $799.99, the short battery life and single-band GPS were harder to accept. At $499.99, you get a sapphire display, titanium caseback, flashlight, maps, music, and full Garmin health tracking for much less than a Fenix 8, which starts above $1,000, and less than the Forerunner 970 at $749. Prices can change, so check the Amazon listing before you buy. Bloomingdale's lists a customer rating of 4.2 out of 5 from 140 reviews, with praise for the display and comfort, and mixed views on battery life.

## What to Know Before You Buy the Garmin Venu X1

The Venu X1 is not perfect, and the gaps matter for some buyers. It uses single-band GPS rather than multi-band GPS, so it may be less precise in dense cities or deep tree cover than Garmin's top endurance watches. It has no ECG and no cellular option, and Tech Advisor found raise to wake could be a little slow. It also cannot match an Apple Watch for smart features such as messaging and voice commands. If you want the longest battery life Garmin makes, or the most precise GPS, look at the Forerunner 970 or Fenix 8 instead. If you want a comfortable, good-looking Garmin with a huge screen for maps, workouts, and daily health, the Venu X1 fits that brief well.

## Frequently Asked Questions

Q: How long does the Garmin Venu X1 battery last?
A: Garmin rates it for up to 8 days in smartwatch mode, 2 days with always-on display, and up to 16 hours in GPS-only mode.

Q: Is the Garmin Venu X1 waterproof?
A: It is rated 5ATM, which covers swimming in a pool or open water, but it is not made for diving.

Q: Is the Garmin Venu X1 worth $499.99?
A: In our view, yes, if you value the large AMOLED display, slim fit, and full Garmin tracking. At its $799.99 launch price it was a harder call, but at $499.99 it is far better value.

guides.title: Uproot Clean Pet Hair Remover Review: Does It Really Work?
guides.excerpt: Our Uproot Clean Pet Hair Remover review looks at how the Pro pulls embedded fur from carpets, rugs and upholstery, and where it falls short.
guides.content:
If you live with a dog or a cat, you already know the pattern. You vacuum, the carpet looks clean, and then the light hits it at a different angle and the hair is still there, pressed flat into the fibres. That is the problem the Uproot Clean Pet Hair Remover Pro is made for, and it is also why it has become one of the most talked about pet hair tools on Amazon. In this Uproot Clean Pet Hair Remover review, we look at what the Pro does well, where it struggles, and whether it is worth a place in your cleaning cupboard. We have not tested it ourselves, so everything here comes from retailer listings and independent reviews published in 2026, not from a hands-on trial.

## What the Uproot Clean Pet Hair Remover Pro actually is

The Pro is a small handheld tool with a metal scraping edge and a plastic handle. There is no motor, no battery and nothing to plug in, and you do not need sticky sheets or refills. You hold it at an angle and drag it across fabric in short, firm strokes, and the edge catches hair that has worked its way down into the weave. PetLovers, which reviewed the tool in March 2026, describes the same idea in simple terms: friction, not suction, is what lifts the hair. The maker lists it for carpets, rugs, clothes, furniture and bedding, but the reviews tell a narrower story, and that narrower story is more useful when you are deciding whether to buy it. At only 2.08 ounces, according to one detailed review, it is light enough to use on stairs and car seats without your wrist getting tired quickly.

## Does the Uproot Clean Pet Hair Remover really work?

On carpets and rugs, the short answer from most reviewers is yes. PetLovers rated it excellent on carpets and rugs, and good on sturdy furniture. Several independent reviewers say the same thing in different words: a carpet that looked clean after vacuuming can still give up a surprising pile of hair after a few passes with the Pro. One reviewer who writes about life with black cats said the tool pulled fur from a cat tree seat that regular cleaning had left behind, and kept finding more on a second pass. That fits the way the tool is built. Vacuums are good at surface dirt, but hair that has been walked on and pressed into carpet fibres can stay put. A metal edge dragged across the surface can roll that hair into clumps you can pick up and throw away. It takes a bit of effort, especially on thick pile, but for that one job it does something a vacuum often does not.

## Where the Uproot Clean Pro works best, and where to skip it

The Pro earns its keep in a few clear places. Stairs, car footwells and trunk liners, cushion seams and the edges of rugs are where reviewers keep coming back to it, because those are the spots a vacuum head cannot reach properly. It also works well on sturdy upholstery in canvas, polyester or tightly woven cotton.

- Carpets and rugs, especially low to medium pile where hair sits deep in the fibres.
- Car interiors, including floor mats, trunk liners and fabric seats.
- Sturdy sofas and chairs, and pet beds with a firm woven cover.
- Stairs and corners, where the small head fits better than a vacuum.

Keep it away from delicate fabrics. Petco warns that it is not for berber carpet, cashmere, or delicate, knitted or woven fabrics, and other reviewers give the same warning for silk, loose linen, velvet and wool sweaters. The metal edge can snag threads and cause pilling, so test a hidden corner first and stop if fibres start to lift. It is also not the best tool for clothes. A lint roller is quicker and safer there, and most reviewers suggest keeping the Pro for the house and the car.

## Uproot Clean Pro vs lint rollers and vacuums

It helps to think of the Pro as a second tool, not a replacement. A vacuum still does the everyday job across a whole room, and a lint roller is still the fastest way to clean a jacket before you walk out the door. The Pro sits in between. It is reusable, so there is nothing to throw away after each use, and it costs about the same as a few packs of roller refills. PetSmart lists it at $16.99, with a 4.3 out of 5 star rating from 18,387 reviews, while Petco lists it at $14.99 with a similar 4.3 star rating. Prices vary by retailer and by Amazon seller, so check the current Amazon price before you buy. Some reviewers also note that the plastic handle can feel light or flimsy during long sessions, which is worth knowing if you plan to clean a whole house in one go.

## Our pick

Uproot Clean Pet Hair Remover Pro

ASIN: B09LNX88YK

Price: around $15 to $17 at PetSmart and Petco in third-party checks in November 2026; Amazon price varies by seller, so check the listing.

Rating: 4.3 out of 5 stars from 18,387 reviews on the PetSmart listing.

Amazon link: https://www.amazon.com/dp/B09LNX88YK

If most of your pet hair problem is on carpets, rugs and car seats, this is the version to start with. It is cheap, simple and easy to store, and it does one job well. If you mainly need to clean clothes, or you have a lot of delicate fabric at home, a lint roller and a good vacuum will serve you better.

## Uproot Clean Pet Hair Remover FAQ

Is the Uproot Clean Pro safe for all carpets? No. Avoid berber carpet and delicate fabrics, and always test a hidden area first. It works best on low to medium pile carpet, rugs and sturdy upholstery.

Do you need batteries or refills for the Uproot Clean Pro? No. It is a manual, reusable tool with no motor, no batteries and no sticky sheets to replace. You just scrape the hair into clumps and pick them up.

Can the Uproot Clean Pro replace a vacuum? No, and reviewers are clear on this point. It works best as a second step after vacuuming, to lift embedded hair that the vacuum leaves behind, especially on stairs, edges and car interiors.

guides.excerpt: Our Owala SmoothSip Slider review covers its leak-proof sliding lid, 20 oz size, hot and cold retention, and whether the $29.99 tumbler is worth it.
guides.content:
Owala built a loyal following with the FreeSip water bottle, and the SmoothSip Slider is the coffee version of that same idea: a simple, good-looking tumbler that is meant to go everywhere with you. It keeps showing up in Amazon best-seller lists, and it has picked up a lot of fans among commuters and coffee drinkers. In this Owala SmoothSip Slider review, we look at what it is, how it performs, and who it suits best. We have not tested it ourselves, so the details here come from the Amazon listing, retailer pages and third-party reviews checked in November 2026, not from a hands-on trial.

## What is the Owala SmoothSip Slider?

The SmoothSip Slider is an insulated stainless steel coffee tumbler with a sliding lid. The version in this review is the 20 oz model in Vanilla Bean, ASIN B0DF49ML4P, which is listed at $29.99. Other sizes are sold too, including a 12 oz version and a 24 oz version with a handle, and the price changes with size and colour, so it is worth checking the exact variant you want. The body is made from 18/8 food-grade stainless steel with double-wall vacuum insulation. Owala says it keeps drinks hot for up to 6 hours and cold for up to 24 hours. The lid is BPA-free and phthalate-free, and the SmoothSip spout is shaped to feel comfortable to drink from, without the splash you get from a wide open mug.

## Owala SmoothSip Slider review: does the leak-proof lid work?

The lid is the main reason people buy this tumbler, and it is also the feature reviewers praise most. When the slider is closed, Owala calls the lid completely leak-proof, and Amazon review summaries picked up by ShopTheSpark in November 2026 show leak-proofing as one of the most mentioned positives, with around 950 mentions. That matters if you throw a tumbler into a bag, leave it on its side in the car, or carry it on a busy train. The slider itself is easy to open and close with one hand, which is handy when you are driving or walking. It does not have a separate lock, so it is best to make sure the slider is fully shut before you toss it in a bag. Temperature retention is the other strong point, with more than 1,100 review mentions and mostly positive feedback, according to the same Amazon review summary.

## How the Owala SmoothSip Slider fits daily life

A tumbler only earns its place if it fits the rest of your routine, and this one is built around that idea. The tapered base fits standard car cup holders, and reviewers note that it also fits under a Keurig spout, which makes it easy to fill in the morning without pouring coffee into a second cup. Twelve ounces is a standard mug of coffee, so the smaller size suits a normal brew, while the 20 oz version here gives you room for iced coffee, a larger latte, or a long drive without a refill. The cup is hand-wash only, while the lid is top-rack dishwasher safe, so cleaning takes a minute but it is not a chore you can skip. Owala also offers a limited lifetime warranty from the manufacturer, which is worth keeping in mind if you plan to use it every day.

## What to watch out for before you buy

No tumbler is perfect, and the SmoothSip Slider has one clear weak spot: durability. In the Amazon review breakdown shared by ShopTheSpark, durability was the least positive theme, with only about 53 percent positive mentions out of around 365. Some buyers say their tumbler has lasted for years, while others report dents, or paint chipping soon after it arrives. That does not mean every cup will chip, but it is a good reason to check the finish as soon as it arrives, so any problem can go through Amazon returns while it is still fresh. The hand-wash rule is the other trade-off. If you want a cup you can put straight in the dishwasher after every use, this is not it. At $29.99 for the 20 oz version, with a 4.6 out of 5 star rating from more than 16,000 ratings in third-party checks, it still sits in a fair price range for a well-made insulated tumbler, but the price does vary by size and colour.

## Our pick

Amazon link: https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0DF49ML4P

If you want a leak-proof coffee tumbler for the car, the office or a daily commute, and you do not mind hand-washing the cup, the SmoothSip Slider is an easy pick at this price. It is at its best as a daily coffee cup, not as a bottle to throw around. If you need a tougher cup for hiking or a job site, look for something with a thicker finish and full dishwasher-safe care first.

How long does the Owala SmoothSip Slider keep drinks hot or cold? Owala rates it at up to 6 hours hot and up to 24 hours cold, thanks to double-wall vacuum insulation. Real results will vary with how full the cup is and how often you open the lid.

Is the Owala SmoothSip Slider really leak-proof? Owala calls the closed slider lid completely leak-proof, and leak-proofing is one of the strongest themes in Amazon reviews. Make sure the slider is fully closed before you put it in a bag, and check the seal if it ever feels loose.

guides.title: iRESTORE Hair Growth System Review: What to Know Before You Buy
guides.excerpt: Thinking about the iRESTORE Hair Growth System Elite? We explain how its laser and LED helmet works, who it suits, what it costs, and what to check first.
guides.content:
Hair thinning is a slow, personal thing. You notice it in photos first, then in the shower drain, and then you start weighing options that range from cheap shampoos to clinic treatments. The iRESTORE Hair Growth System Elite sits near the premium end of the at home options. In this iRESTORE hair growth system review, we explain what the device actually is, who it is most likely to suit, and the questions worth asking before you spend this kind of money.

## What the iRESTORE Elite is

The Elite is a hands free, helmet shaped device that uses low level light therapy, sometimes called photobiomodulation. It combines 300 lasers and 200 LEDs, 500 diodes in total, in three red wavelengths: 625, 655 and 680 nm. Sessions take 12 minutes, once a day, and the device is meant to be worn at home while you get on with something else. It is FDA cleared under 510(k) K222081, from October 2022, for androgenetic alopecia, which is the pattern hair loss many adults experience. FDA clearance is not the same as a guarantee that it will work for you, and it does not mean it treats every kind of hair loss.

## What the evidence does and does not say

This is the part to read slowly. The brand points to a clinical trial in which participants had a 43 percent increase in mature hair count compared with a placebo helmet over 16 weeks. That sounds strong, and it is worth knowing, but it is the brand's own trial, and individual results vary a lot with hair loss. Independent reviewers have been more measured. Wareable rated the Elite 4.5 out of 5 after several months of use, and noted that progress was gradual and subtle. One magazine tester saw visible change while also using other hair products, so the helmet's share of the result was unclear. We have not tested this device ourselves, and we are not going to promise regrowth. Light therapy has credible supporting research, but no home device can promise a result for a specific person.

## Price, guarantee and the fine print

The Elite is a premium purchase, and prices move around. Recent third party checks in November 2026 put it from about $1,799, with a wireless battery option costing about $99 extra, while one review of the brand's own store listed it at $2,699. We could not verify the current Amazon price at the time of writing, so treat any price here as a guide and check the listing before you buy. What seems consistent is the aftercare: a 12 month money back guarantee and a 3 year warranty, according to recent reviews. One review also reported that the parent company holds an F rating from the Better Business Bureau, while the brand's own Trustpilot page sits around 3.4 out of 5 from more than 900 reviews. That mixed picture does not settle the question, but it is worth knowing before you commit.

## Who it suits, and who should pause

The Elite makes most sense for someone who caught their hair thinning early, is happy to commit to a 12 minute session every day for months, and can afford a premium device without stretching the budget. It is less suited to anyone who wants a quick fix, dislikes wearing a helmet, or is dealing with sudden hair loss, patchy loss, scarring, or a scalp condition. If your hair loss has a medical cause, or you are unsure what is causing it, talk to a doctor or dermatologist first. They can help work out whether light therapy fits your situation. That conversation matters more than any review, including this one.

## Our pick

## FAQ

How long does each iRESTORE Elite session take? Each session takes 12 minutes, once a day. The key point is consistency over months, not a single long session.

Will the iRESTORE Elite regrow my hair? No one can promise that. The brand cites a clinical trial showing an increase in mature hair count, and reviewers report gradual change at best. Talk to a doctor first if your hair loss is medical.

Is the iRESTORE Elite FDA cleared? Yes, it is FDA cleared under 510(k) K222081 for androgenetic alopecia. Clearance means the device was shown to be as safe and effective as similar cleared devices, not that it works for everyone.

guides.title: COSORI Stainless Steel Air Fryer Review: Is the 6.5-Quart Worth It?
guides.excerpt: Is the COSORI Iconic stainless steel air fryer worth $249? We break down its 6.5-quart capacity, PFAS-free ceramic basket and real owner ratings.
guides.content:
Most air fryers look the same once you have owned one for a while. A plastic shell, a nonstick basket that starts to wear, and a price that feels fair until you start wondering what is actually touching your food. The COSORI Iconic Stainless Steel Air Fryer takes a different route. It wraps a 6.5-quart basket in stainless steel, swaps the usual PTFE coating for a ceramic surface Cosori says is free of PFAS, PTFE and BPA, and charges $249 for the privilege. That is a lot of money for a single-basket air fryer, so the real question is simple. Does the build quality justify the price, or are you paying for a prettier box?

## What you actually get for $249

The headline specs are easy to list. You get a 6.5-quart basket that Cosori rates for three to five people, a 1,725-watt heating element, and a temperature range of 90 to 450 degrees Fahrenheit. Six functions cover the usual ground: Air Fry, Roast, Bake, Dry, Proof and Reheat. A DC motor runs the fan at five speeds, which matters more than it sounds, because steady airflow is what keeps one side of your fries from going soft while the other side burns.

The materials are the real story here. Cosori says 96 percent of the visible surface is metal, with a 430-grade stainless steel body and a 304 stainless steel basket finished in ceramic. The control panel is tempered glass, and the whole thing weighs about 14 pounds. It is a big unit, roughly 15 inches deep, so measure your counter and your cabinet clearance before you order. Fingerprints show up fast on the steel, which is the kind of small annoyance that only bothers you once you have paid premium money.

## How the COSORI Iconic air fryer cooks

On cooking performance, the independent testing we found is encouraging. RTINGS scored the Iconic 7.9 out of 10 for air frying, and reviewers who cooked with it report crisp, evenly browned fries, chicken and vegetables. The 450-degree ceiling helps here. Most air fryers top out at 400, and that extra heat is what gives chicken skin and roast vegetables a proper finish instead of a pale one.

Owners seem happy too. As of November 18, 2026, the Iconic held 4.6 stars from 362 Amazon ratings, which is a solid score for a new model at this price. The basket is roomy enough for a 9-inch pizza, and the shake reminder on the touch panel is a small touch that genuinely helps with even cooking. The VeSync app adds guided recipes and lets you send time and temperature to the fryer from your phone, plus Alexa and Google voice control. One honest limit: you still have to press Start on the machine itself, so there is no remote cooking while you are out.

## Who should buy the COSORI Iconic, and who should skip it

This fryer makes the most sense if the cooking surface matters to you. If you have been looking for a PFAS-free air fryer with a steel body and you cook for three or more people most nights, the Iconic is one of the few options that ticks every box, and the five-year warranty backs that up. Cosori launched it in January 2026 at $249, and it is still the most expensive single-basket model in the lineup.

If price is your main concern, be honest with yourself and skip it. Cosori's own TurboBlaze costs roughly half as much, and RTINGS actually scored it slightly higher for air frying, at 8.2. You lose the steel body and the ceramic basket, but the food comes out about the same. That is the whole decision in one sentence: you are paying for materials and longevity, not for dramatically better cooking.

guides.title: Ninja Thirsti Pink Review: Flavored Water Without the Sugar?
guides.excerpt: The pink Ninja Thirsti turns plain water into flavored sparkling drinks at home. We look at its price, flavors, fizz settings and running costs.
guides.content:
Plain water is fine. Most of us just do not drink enough of it, and a can of soda is a lot more tempting than a glass of tap water at 3 in the afternoon. The Ninja Thirsti Pink is built for that exact moment. It is a countertop drink system that carbonates your water and adds flavor from small pods, so you get something that tastes like a treat without the sugar crash. The pink finish is new for 2026, joining the original stone color, and it looks sharp on a counter. But a pretty machine is not enough. The real question is whether the drinks taste good, what it costs to keep running, and whether you will still use it in three months.

## How the Ninja Thirsti Pink works

The idea is simple, and the order of operations matters. The Thirsti carbonates your water first, then adds flavor, which is why the fizz stays consistent from the first sip to the last. You fill the 48-ounce removable reservoir with cold water, load a 60L CO2 cylinder into the back, pop in one or two flavor pods, and pick your settings. Four size settings run from 6 ounces up to a full pour, and you can choose still water or three levels of fizz, plus classic or bold flavor strength. You can even mix two flavors to make your own blend.

Ninja says there are more than 20 zero and low-calorie flavors, from fruit splashes and iced teas to sodas and energy drinks with caffeine. The Splash flavors are unsweetened, a lot like a canned sparkling water, while the sweeter drops use sucralose. That split matters, because the unsweetened ones tend to get the best reviews and the sweet ones can leave an aftertaste if you go bold on the flavor.

## What the Ninja Thirsti Pink costs, now and later

The base unit is the part you need to price carefully. SharkNinja lists the pink WC3001PK1 at $179.99, and we saw it at $129.99 on the SharkNinja site during our research, so the price does move around. On Amazon the price was not verified at the time of writing, so check the listing before you buy. What the box includes is the drink station itself, the 48-ounce reservoir and one 60L CO2 cylinder. Flavor pods are sold separately, so your first order needs pods or the machine just makes very nice plain sparkling water.

Then come the running costs. A bottle of Flavored Drops sells for about $6.99 and makes roughly 17 to 20 twelve-ounce drinks. A 60L CO2 cylinder carbonates around 100 twelve-ounce drinks and costs about $36.99 to replace, with a discount if you send the empty one back for recycling. If you drink a flavored sparkling water every day, the machine pays for itself against canned seltzer eventually, but it is not instant.

## The catch: you are locked into Ninja flavors

Here is the part to think about before you buy. The Thirsti only takes Ninja's own flavor pods. You cannot pour in your own syrup, juice or a flavor from another brand, because the machine carbonates water only and adds flavor from its own cartridges. If you love experimenting with your own syrups, a SodaStream-style setup gives you more freedom.

The other thing to know is the rating. On the SharkNinja site, the pink model holds about 4.2 stars from 252 reviews. That is decent rather than glowing, and it fits what reviewers say overall: the machine does its job well, the fizz is strong and consistent, and the flavor quality varies by pod. Start with the unsweetened Splash flavors if you are unsure, and try one sweet flavor before stocking up.

## Our pick

The Amazon price was not verified at the time of writing, so treat the SharkNinja list price of $179.99 as a guide and compare. guides.title: Amazfit Cheetah 2 Ultra Review: A $599.99 Running Watch Worth It?
guides.excerpt: Is the $599.99 Amazfit Cheetah 2 Ultra worth it for runners? We break down its titanium build, GPS accuracy, battery life and trail features.
guides.content:
The Amazfit Cheetah 2 Ultra is a serious running watch with a serious price tag. At $599.99, it sits in the same conversation as watches from Garmin and Coros, and that is exactly the comparison it invites. So the real question is not whether it looks the part. It does, with a titanium body and a bright sapphire-covered display. The question is whether the running experience behind it justifies six hundred dollars, and for which runners the answer is yes.

We have not tested this watch ourselves, so this review pulls together the published specs and the independent checks we could verify. That matters here because the Cheetah 2 Ultra is still new, having launched in May 2026, and owner ratings are thin. Target lists it at $599.99 with 4.5 out of 5 stars, but from only two ratings, which tells us almost nothing on its own. WIRED gave it 7 out of 10, praising its sports and mapping features and battery life while calling out the busy software and the high price. Keep those caveats in mind as you read on.

## Amazfit Cheetah 2 Ultra specs and build quality

The headline specs are genuinely premium. You get a 1.5-inch AMOLED display at 480 x 480 pixels with up to 3,000 nits of peak brightness, covered by sapphire glass. In plain terms, it should stay readable in harsh midday sun, which is where cheaper running watches start to struggle. The case uses a Grade 5 titanium bezel, frame, back cover and buttons, with a fibre-reinforced polymer case, and the whole thing weighs 52 grams without the strap. That is light for a 47.4 mm watch, and on a long run the weight on your wrist is something you notice.

Inside, there is 64 GB of storage for offline maps and music, a BioTracker PPG sensor for heart rate and blood oxygen, and more than 180 sports modes. Water resistance is rated at 5 ATM, which covers swimming and heavy rain but is worth noting if you were hoping for a 10 ATM rating at this price. It runs Zepp OS and connects over Bluetooth 5.2 and Wi-Fi. There is no LTE, so this is a phone-companion watch rather than a standalone one.

## Amazfit Cheetah 2 Ultra battery life

Battery life is one of the strongest reasons to look at this watch. Amazfit rates the 780 mAh battery at up to 30 days of typical use, up to 60 hours in accuracy GPS mode, up to 33 hours in trail running mode, and up to 228 hours in maximum GPS mode. Those are the maker's figures, and real life will vary with how often you run with GPS and how bright you keep the screen.

Independent testing from the5krunner projected around 55 hours in full-accuracy GPS mode, which lines up well with the official 60-hour claim. For most runners that means a full week of training on one charge without thinking about it, and for ultrarunners it means the watch can survive a very long race day. If you are coming from a smartwatch that needs charging every night, this is the single biggest quality-of-life change the Ultra offers.

## Amazfit Cheetah 2 Ultra GPS and trail running features

The Ultra earns its name mainly on the trail. It uses dual-band GPS across six satellite systems with a circularly-polarised antenna, and the5krunner scored its GPS at 85 percent on a standard 10-mile test. That put it ahead of the Cheetah 2 Pro at 73 percent, though behind the Coros and Garmin leaders in the same test. Heart rate tracking also did well in that testing, with five excellent results and one good across six sessions.

What sets the Ultra apart from the cheaper Cheetah 2 Pro is a set of trail-specific tools: a dedicated trail running mode, a terrain load factor, and an Elevation Overview. For road runners the feature set is otherwise the same as the Pro, so the Ultra is really aimed at people who run trails and ultras. If your running is mostly roads and parks, you are paying for trail features you may never open.

## Who should buy the Amazfit Cheetah 2 Ultra?

This watch makes the most sense for trail runners and ultrarunners who want long GPS battery life, a big readable screen, and a light titanium build without paying Garmin flagship prices. It also suits data-hungry runners who want offline maps and music on the wrist, plus detailed training and elevation metrics.

It makes less sense if you want a polished everyday smartwatch. The Zepp OS interface has been criticised as busy, and the smartwatch side, things like apps and voice assistants, is weaker than what Apple or Samsung offer. It also makes less sense for casual runners. At $599.99, a cheaper Cheetah model or a mid-range Garmin will cover most road-running needs for a lot less money.

Is the Amazfit Cheetah 2 Ultra good for road running? Yes, it covers road running well, with accurate GPS and heart rate tracking in independent testing. But road runners get the same core features from the cheaper Cheetah 2 Pro, so the Ultra is harder to justify unless you also run trails.

guides.title: Boxiecat Probiotic Cat Litter Review: Does It Really Control Odor?
guides.excerpt: Does Boxiecat Probiotic Cat Litter really control odor for 40 days? We look at its probiotic clumping clay, dust, clumps and real owner ratings.
guides.content:
Cat litter is one of those household buys where a small difference shows up every single day. A litter that clumps well means less waste and less scrubbing. A litter that actually controls odor means a fresher home. Boxiecat Probiotic Cat Litter promises both, with a twist: instead of covering smells with perfume, it adds probiotics that are meant to break down the bacteria behind the odor. It sounds clever, and the idea is borrowed from the same science behind enzymatic cleaners. But does it work in a real litter box, and is it worth the premium over ordinary clay?

This is a research-based review. We have not tested this litter at home, so everything here comes from the maker's published specs, retailer listings, and independent review sites that did test it. We could not verify an Amazon star rating for this exact 16 lb listing, since Amazon blocks direct access, so where we quote ratings we say clearly where they came from. Petco lists the 16 lb bag at $23.99, and its listing shows an overall rating of 4.5 out of 5 from 467 reviews, though that figure appears to cover the product line rather than this one bag size alone.

## How Boxiecat Probiotic Cat Litter works

Boxiecat is an unscented clumping clay litter. The probiotic blend is a mix of harmless microorganisms that, according to the maker, consume the odor-causing bacteria in waste and keep working between scoops. The idea is to cut ammonia off at the source rather than masking it with fragrance. The litter is also marketed as 99.9 percent dust-free and hypoallergenic, with no added fragrances, fillers or preservatives, which matters if anyone in the house, cat or human, is sensitive to dust or scent.

The maker claims up to 40 days of odor control and says the litter lasts about twice as long as other litters. Those are best-case claims, and it is worth treating them that way. More cats in the house and less frequent scooping will shorten any litter's odor control, probiotics or not. No litter removes the need to scoop daily, and Boxiecat is no exception.

## Boxiecat Probiotic Cat Litter clumping and dust

Clumping is where Boxiecat earns most of its praise. It forms hard, flat-topped clumps that set near the surface, so you can lift them out without scraping the bottom of the pan. That matters more than it sounds. Clumps that break apart leave damp litter behind, and that leftover waste is what makes a box smell stale even after scooping.

Independent testing at Review Cat Litter found that 94 percent of Boxiecat's clumps survived a drop test, and measured dust at just 0.04 mg per pour, roughly level with Dr. Elsey's Ultra. That is a genuinely low dust result, and owners in reviews repeatedly mention the low dust as a reason they stay with the brand. Some owners have reported newer batches running finer and dustier, though, so the experience may vary from bag to bag.

## Does Boxiecat Probiotic Cat Litter really control odor?

Here the picture is more mixed, and it is the part of this review that matters most. In a 28-day ammonia monitoring test, Review Cat Litter gave Boxiecat an odor control score of 8.7 out of 10, with ammonia staying low for the first two weeks and rising to 20 ppm by week four. Their key finding was that the probiotic effect faded after about three weeks once the bag had been open and exposed to air. The bacteria, once exposed to air and litter box conditions, gradually die off.

That lines up with what Indoor Cat Lab found in its research-based review, which gave Boxiecat an overall score of 8.1 out of 10. Its verdict was that Boxiecat suits owners who want an unscented clay that scoops cleanly, but that some owners report weaker control of feces odor than urine odor, and that owner ratings sit a little below some big-name clays. So the honest answer is that the odor control is good at first and genuinely better than scented cover-ups, but the 40-day claim is optimistic, especially in a multi-cat home.

## Who should buy Boxiecat Probiotic Cat Litter?

This litter is a good fit if you want an unscented litter, if dust bothers you or your cat, and if broken clumps are your main complaint. The flat-top clumping is the strongest thing about it, and it genuinely reduces waste and full litter changes. It is also a sensible pick if you dislike perfumed litter and want odor control that works without fragrance in the house.

It is a weaker fit for a heavily used multi-cat box, where the probiotic effect fades and the premium price adds up fast. At around $23.99 for 16 lb at Petco, it costs noticeably more per pound than mainstream clay, so a large household will feel that difference every month. If your main problem is tracking, note that some owners report litter tracked outside the box, so a good litter mat is worth having.

How long does Boxiecat Probiotic Cat Litter control odor? The maker claims up to 40 days. Independent testing found strong odor control for the first two weeks, with the probiotic effect fading after about three weeks of the bag being open. Daily scooping and the number of cats using the box make a big difference.
